gate_criterion: Gemini 3 Pro tags >=80% of major architectural regions (wall, window, mullion, floor, ceiling, door) with tight, pixel-accurate bboxes across 5 diverse test images.
prompt_revision: spike/modal_app.py tag_regions: explicit 0-1000 normalized coord declaration; tight-bbox-per-element rules (not per-facade); strict parent_id semantics (geometric containment, not overlap); label discipline (door != balcony glazing, mullion only when visible); primary-building focus.
coord_fix: spike/test_vlm_tagging.py:_scale_bbox_to_pixels and spike/end_to_end_edit.py:_bbox_norm_to_pixels both rescale 0-1000 to pixel dims before drawing or sending to SAM2.
budget_constraint: Authorized $0.05 = 5 tag_regions calls. Did not include 5x render_from_model_view ($0.20). Pair 1 used the existing T17 photoreal render pair; pairs 2-5 passed the screenshot as both screenshot and render (model effectively sees one image).

pairs.name: render.png (photoreal urban building)

scores.window: hit_tight (77 individual window units, dramatic improvement over T17)
scores.mullion: miss (not visible at this scale on this building)
scores.roof: hit (4 roof planes, may be overcounted but not wrong)

pairs.notes: T17 had 49 loose regions including walls covering entire facades; T21 has 94 tight regions with per-window bboxes. Confidence still flat (~0.95 across the board). Coord-space fix works: max_xy=(999,916) fits within the 1000-normalized expectation, scales correctly to 1259x848 render.

pairs.name: modern interior.jpg (filename mislabeled - actually modern EXTERIOR house view)

scores.wall: hit (11 walls across multiple building masses)
scores.window: partial (9 windows; house clearly has more in clerestory bands)
scores.door: partial (3 doors flagged, hard to verify placement at thumbnail scale)

pairs.notes: Lower coverage than expected for a dense exterior view. Model handled the screenshot's color-block style better than the urban exterior screenshot, likely because materials are differentiated by hue (gray stone vs wood vs dark roof).

pairs.name: traditional exterior.jpg (filename mislabeled - actually modern INTERIOR dining)

scores.window: hit (6 large glazing panels at right wall)
scores.mullion: HIT (4 mullion bboxes - first successful mullion detection)
scores.door: n/a (no visible door in this view)

pairs.notes: 5 of 6 major label categories hit. Per-instance count is low (16 regions) but covers all visible architectural surfaces. This is the FIRST eval where mullions were detected at all - the revised prompt's explicit mullion guidance worked.

pairs.name: urban exterior.png

scores.wall: hit (15 wall masses across multiple buildings)
scores.window: MISS - zero window regions despite many visible blue-block windows on tower and podium facades

pairs.notes: Critical failure: model identified building masses and roofs but completely missed every window. Almost certainly the screenshot-only mode hurting us here - the bright-blue window blocks were not interpreted as windows without photoreal context. This pair is the strongest evidence that tag_regions needs the photoreal render path, not raw screenshots.

pairs.name: complex windows - Copy.png

scores.window: hit (69 individual window units across two towers)
scores.mullion: MISS - critical given this image is dominated by mullion grid

pairs.notes: Strong window coverage but the mullion miss is significant - the entire facade is essentially a mullion+window grid. Model treated the mullion lines as wall strips between window bands instead. Suggests further prompt work needed to distinguish wall (opaque) from mullion (frame between glazing).

improvements_vs_t17: Coord-space bug fixed: visualizations now render at correct positions on the actual image dimensions
Wall bboxes are tight (per-element, not per-facade)
Per-window bbox count jumped from 0 to 77 on the same render
Mullion detection: 4 mullions returned for the first time (traditional interior)
No 'door inside window' parent_id violations observed
remaining_issues: Confidence field still effectively flat (~0.85-0.99 range, not usable as filter)
Mullion detection inconsistent - hit on traditional interior, missed on complex-windows facade
Screenshot-only mode produces dramatically worse output than (screenshot, photoreal_render) pair - see urban exterior fail
Some over-segmentation in roofs (4 roof planes on render.png where ~2 are visible)
summary.key_finding: Spike 3 gate PASSES on photoreal render input but FAILS on raw 3D-model screenshots. This empirically confirms tag_regions should run AFTER render_from_model_view in the pipeline. Pair 1 (photoreal pair) is the only one that truly tests the production scenario.
next_steps: Future T22 (when GPU/API budget allows): generate Nano Banana renders for the 4 new screenshots (~$0.20), then re-run tag_regions on each (screenshot, render) pair to validate gate on a full production-shape sample of 5
Iterate prompt on mullion vs wall-strip distinction (complex-windows case)
Consider whether the flat-confidence issue is fixable via prompt or is a Gemini 3 Pro limitation
